cohort: Not applicable. The package never reads any data file: no read_csv/read_excel/open of AI-Hub partitions, no subject list, no MMSE/cognitive file. `ShapAnalyzer.__init__` receives an already-trained model plus feature names (analyzer.py:59-72) and `explain(X)` receives whatever array the caller passes (analyzer.py:112-129). Both directories are byte-identical (`diff -rq` excluding __pycache__ exits 0), so one audit covers both.
record_count: Not applicable. N is simply the row count of the caller-supplied X (analyzer.py:114, 260-264). No merge, dedup or filter code exists anywhere in the 7 files.
label: Not applicable. No label column is read or mapped. The package default is a 3-class task: `task="multiclass"`, `n_classes=3` (analyzer.py:65-66), and USAGE.md:42 / :78 document class_names ["CN","MCI","Dementia"]. `task="binary"` is accepted but only changes how the SHAP output axis is sliced (analyzer.py:306-307).
record_construction: Not applicable. No activity/sleep pairing, date join, or duplicate handling. `_coerce_input` only converts X to ndarray and an optional DataFrame view (analyzer.py:283-296).
missing_values: Not applicable. No imputer, dropna, or NaN handling anywhere; X is passed through to shap unchanged (explainers.py:41-43, 67-70).
features: Not applicable. Feature names are an opaque list supplied by the caller (analyzer.py:82); the only check is a length match against the SHAP array (outputs.py:43-47). No sleep_time, clock conversion, 1-min MET statistics, 5-min class counts or hypnogram counts are computed. USAGE.md:109 refers to an LSTM input of shape (N, 7, 71), i.e. a 71-feature multiclass ML4 pipeline, not the paper's 72.
feature_selection: No forward selection exists. What the package provides is only the SHAP importance step: `shap.TreeExplainer(model)` with default arguments, i.e. tree_path_dependent (explainers.py:39); `shap.GradientExplainer` for Keras models (explainers.py:65); importance = mean |SHAP| over the explained rows plus a mean signed SHAP (outputs.py:50-52); with `combine_classes=False` the per-class mean |SHAP| values are averaged across all classes (analyzer.py:179-186). SHAP is computed on whatever X the caller passes (USAGE.md:45 and :82 show X_test). No k, no ranking-then-refit loop.
split: Not applicable. No KFold/StratifiedKFold/GroupKFold, no seeds for splitting (the only `random_state` is for sampling the Keras background set, analyzer.py:259-264), no hold-out, no nesting. Grep for "Cheon", "forward selection", "전진 선택" returns no file under xai/.
model_and_hyperparameters: Not applicable. No model is trained; `detect_model_type` only classifies an already-fitted object as "tree" or "keras_sequence" (detect.py:34-60). Table 2 values (min_data_in_leaf 41, num_leaves 330, n_estimators 1000, learning_rate 0.08) do not appear. No grid search.
statistics: Not applicable. No fold scores, no CI, no threshold, no AUC computation in these files.
reported_results: None. USAGE.md contains only illustrative example values (e.g. USAGE.md:172 mean_abs_shap 0.0421) and no ROC-AUC or other performance number. No outputs/ or results directory exists under either xai/ folder.

potential_errors.description: Binary task with an older shap that returns a list of two arrays: `_to_ndarray` stacks the list into shape (2, N, F), `_slice_classes` returns it unchanged for task='binary', and `aggregate_time_axis` then treats axis 1 (the sample axis) as a time axis. `importance_dataframe` subsequently averages over the two class slices, so mean_signed_shap collapses to 0 (class-0 and class-1 SHAP are negatives of each other). mean_abs_shap stays correct. Only affects callers using task='binary' with shap < 0.45-style list output.
potential_errors.evidence: explainers.py:81-82 (stack list -> (C,...)); analyzer.py:306-307 (binary returns [raw]); aggregation.py:39-47 (3D treated as (N,T,F)); outputs.py:50-52

potential_errors.description: For tree models the SHAP importance is computed on whatever X the caller passes; the package itself has no notion of train/test folds, so any leakage (ranking on evaluation rows) is decided entirely by the calling script, not here.

differences_vs_new_implementation: Not a comparable implementation: no cohort (A02), no row-wise pairing (A03), no label file (A04), no feature engineering (A06-A09), no CV (A10), no models (A12), no imputation stance (A13), no forward path (A15-A17), no Table-2 constants (A18), no aggregation rule (A21).

Only overlap is the SHAP step: shap.TreeExplainer default (tree_path_dependent) and mean |SHAP| importance match A14 (explainers.py:39; outputs.py:50), but the package's single-ranking mode averages mean |SHAP| across all classes (analyzer.py:179-186) whereas A14 uses the positive-class mean |SHAP| in a binary setting.
